messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT DETECTED: GPU_POOL_EXHAUSTION in eu-gpu-pool. Autoscaler failing to stabilize. Queue length rising > 12k. Trigger: scale-retry-loop. Pager sent to oncall.
anna (oncall): OMG seeing 503s from hosted api, requestsqueue spike. I’m on it. starting triage.
anna (oncall): querying queue metrics — `sum(request_queue_length) by (pool)` shows eu-gpu-pool at 12.4k and still increasing.
kevin: Confirmed, also seeing steady 429s from provider during scaleup attempts. Provider rate-limit on instance creation.
sandeep: Oncall handoff FYI — I’m joining the bridge in 2m. Current impact: customer-facing gen endpoints degraded; embeddings latencies spiking.
marie: Support: first customer reports inbound. Two mid-market customers seeing timeouts, ticket #CS-1429 and #CS-1430. Notifying them: "we are investigating".
anna (oncall): quick mitigation idea: enable routing fallback to smaller-ram model variant (vm-small) for non-SLA tenants to reduce GPU pressure. Anyone object?
kevin: +1 do it. Also suggest turning on short-lived prefix-KV caching to reduce repeated context compute.
infra-bot: autoscaler logs: `error scaling up: provider quota_reached (429)`, retries exhausted, cooldown extended. Recent change 3 days ago bumped scale_retries to 6.
anna (oncall): temporary manual capacity: can we attach warm spare nodes from reserved pool? `rwdctl capacity attach --pool eu-gpu-pool --from reserved-spare-2 --count 2`
ops-lead: Do it, but keep an eye on tenant fairness. Anna, handoff to you for manual attach.
anna (oncall): running attach now...
anna (oncall): attached 2 spares. pool capacity +2. queue dropped from 12.4k -> 8.1k in 5m.
sandeep: good headroom but still high. We should also reduce per-request concurrency for heavy models: `route-config set concurrency=1 --route /v1/generate-heavy`.
kevin: did that. concurrency set. Also temporarily bumped routing priority to favor dedicated-committed customers.
marie: Customer comms updated: CS-1429 updated with ETA 30m, CS-1430 minor impact, offered workaround to use smaller model for non-critical runs.
anna (oncall): observed autoscaler recently started oscillating: scale up -> provider 429 -> backoff -> cache cold -> more queue -> repeat. Need durable fix not just spares.
sandeep: I’ll open a quick patch to autoscaler: lower aggressive downscale, increase cooldown, and add provider-429 hijack: on 429 during scale up, mark provider unhealthy for 4m and try alternate provider pool.
kevin: Also add a queue-depth based scale target (e.g., target_queue_per_gpu=200) instead of purely CPU utilization. That would have caught this earlier.
ops-lead: Create an immediate mitigation playbook note: fallback routing, attach spares, reduce concurrency, prioritize customers. Then longer-term fixes tracked as action items.
anna (oncall): note: enabled fallback routing to smaller models for 30m window. Enabled KV caching. Reduced concurrency. Attached spares. Re-routed low-priority tenants to burstless pool.
infra-bot: observation: KV cache hit-rate increased from 6% -> 45% after enable. Token cost per request down ~18%.
kevin: queue currently 3.2k and trending down. Latency 95p dropped from 11s -> 2.8s after mitigations.
marie: Support: customers acknowledged. Escalation to enterprise reps for CS-1429 done. No legal/regulatory customers impacted.
anna (oncall): moving to postmortem notes: root cause appears to be a combination of provider quota limits + autoscaler retry policy + reliance on single provider pool for burst capacity. Recent changes to scale_retries made autoscaler hammer provider and then fallback slowly.
sandeep: immediate root-cause summary: autoscaler retry loop on provider 429 led to oscillation; queue depth signal absent; no provider failover on repeated 429s.
kevin: contributing factor: recent config change 3d ago reduced downscale cooldown (faster downscale) which made capacity volatile when requests burst.
ops-lead: Impact: ~45 minutes of degraded service for some customers; 2 enterprise minor incidents opened; internal paging and 6 engineers involved.
marie: Customer impact log: CS-1429 timed-out requests for 38m; CS-1430 intermittent failures for 22m. Compensatory credits TBD.
anna (oncall): Action items (short):
- [A1] Patch autoscaler: treat provider 429 as transient provider-unhealthy, mark failover to alternate provider after 3 consecutive 429s. Owner: sandeep. Due: 48h.
- [A2] Add queue-depth signal to scaling policy and target_queue_per_gpu default to 200. Owner: kevin. Due: 72h.
- [A3] Revert the aggressive downscale cooldown change and set min_cooldown=5m. Owner: infra team. Due: 24h.
- [A4] Update runbook with step "attach reserved-spare nodes" and fallback routing. Owner: ops-lead. Due: 24h.
- [A5] Improve provider quota monitoring/alerts (alert when scale attempts returning >=5 429s in 2m). Owner: infra-bot -> infra. Due: 72h.
- [A6] Customer comms follow-up and credits review. Owner: marie. Due: 48h.
sandeep: I’ll start a PR for A1 now: branch autoscaler/429-failover. Quick test on staging first.
kevin: I’ll wire metrics: queue-depth panel and a synthetic test that simulates provider 429s to validate failover.
ops-lead: schedule postmortem writeup and 1hr review tomorrow. Add retro notes about safer autoscaler defaults.
anna (oncall): final note: good teamwork, we avoided full outage by attaching spares and fallback routing. Recommend we run a chaos test for provider 429s in next sprint.
marie: I’ll draft customer templates and run numbers for credits.
infra-bot: incident resolved: queue back to baseline, autoscaler temporarily paused for config change. Logging incident ID: INC-2026-6379998888.
anna (oncall): closing triage. If anyone sees regression re-open thread. :white_check_mark:
